knowledge_delta.summary: Google SRE refines the project's broad observability concept into an operator decision model: black-box symptoms establish impact, white-box signals support diagnosis, golden signals provide a compact baseline, and pager rules protect human attention through low-noise actionability. The initial retrieval returned no matches despite an existing observability concept, exposing a real prior-knowledge recall miss.

items.label: Observability
items.source_basis: The chapter distinguishes monitoring purposes, black-box symptom detection, white-box diagnosis and strict paging signal/noise boundaries.
items.prior_basis: The cumulative graph already contained a broad observability concept from the enterprise-agent case, but the source scaffold retrieved no prior matches for this monitoring-focused query.
items.interpretation: This manually curated refinement records both the richer operator model and a dogfood retrieval-recall failure that deterministic prior retrieval should eventually learn to catch.

items.label: Black-box monitoring
items.source_basis: The chapter defines black-box monitoring as externally visible behavior seen as a user would see it and emphasizes its value for active symptoms.
items.prior_basis: No prior graph concept separated external symptom monitoring from internal diagnostic telemetry.
items.interpretation: Black-box monitoring becomes the impact-oriented side of the monitoring model.

items.label: White-box monitoring
items.source_basis: White-box monitoring inspects internal metrics/logs/interfaces and helps diagnose causes plus imminent or masked failures.
items.prior_basis: The graph had generic observability but no explicit internal-versus-external monitoring distinction.
items.interpretation: White-box monitoring becomes the diagnosis/prediction side of the model rather than another synonym for observability.

items.label: Four golden signals
items.source_basis: The chapter names latency, traffic, errors and saturation as the four signals to prioritize when only four service-health metrics can be measured.
items.prior_basis: No existing concept provided a compact default service-monitoring vocabulary.
items.interpretation: The golden signals become a reusable baseline, not a complete domain-specific monitoring specification.

items.label: Actionable paging
items.source_basis: The chapter treats paging as expensive human interruption, warns about alert fatigue and favors simple robust rules with high signal and low noise.
items.prior_basis: The graph did not yet represent human-attention cost as an explicit monitoring design constraint.
items.interpretation: Paging becomes a constrained decision surface rather than the automatic endpoint for every telemetry anomaly.

claims.text: Black-box monitoring observes externally visible service behavior and active symptoms, while white-box monitoring uses internal instrumentation to diagnose causes and expose masked or imminent failures.

evidence.locator: Monitoring Distributed Systems → Black-Box Versus White-Box

claims.text: Paging a human is expensive and frequent noisy pages cause responders to skim or ignore alerts, so pager conditions should have high signal, low noise and clear operational meaning.
Latency, traffic, errors and saturation are the four golden signals recommended as a compact baseline when monitoring a user-facing service.

evidence.locator: Monitoring Distributed Systems → The Four Golden Signals

claims.text: Monitoring should distinguish what is broken from why it is broken, because service symptoms and underlying causes serve different roles in detection and diagnosis.

evidence.locator: Monitoring Distributed Systems → Symptoms Versus Causes

claims.text: The source is a genuine refinement of the project's existing observability concept even though the deterministic prior-knowledge scaffold returned no matches for the monitoring query, revealing a retrieval-recall gap rather than absence of prior knowledge.

prerequisite_map.summary: The useful operator model needs four pieces: black-box symptoms for impact, white-box signals for diagnosis, golden signals as a service-health baseline and explicit pager actionability to protect human attention.

items.label: Black-box monitoring
items.reason: The monitoring strategy starts by knowing what users can actually experience rather than only inspecting internal system state.

items.label: White-box monitoring
items.reason: Internal telemetry is the mechanism for diagnosing causes and seeing masked/imminent failures that black-box probes cannot explain.

items.label: Four golden signals
items.reason: Latency, traffic, errors and saturation provide the compact baseline needed before adding service-specific depth.

items.label: Actionable paging
items.reason: Human interruption cost is what turns monitoring from a telemetry problem into an operator decision problem.

learning_prompt.retention_prompt: Without looking back, reconstruct the SRE monitoring model: distinguish a symptom from a cause, explain black-box versus white-box monitoring, name the four golden signals, and state why a useful diagnostic metric should not automatically become a pager alert.

transfer_prompt.prompt: A service has hundreds of internal metrics, frequent pages and user complaints about intermittent latency. Redesign the monitoring decision path: which signals prove user impact, which remain diagnostic, which golden signals anchor service health and what qualifies for paging?

source_decision.rationale: The explainer preserves the operator mental model, but the original chapter is worth opening at three evidence-dense sections: why paging noise matters, black-box versus white-box monitoring, and the four golden signals. The rest of the chapter adds useful measurement depth but is not required for the requested first model.

novelty.reason: The source turns generic observability into an explicit operator signal/diagnosis/paging model and exposes a real prior-retrieval miss.

source_quality.reason: The primary source is the official Google SRE Book chapter authored from production SRE practice.

relevance.reason: The symptom/cause and paging-signal boundaries apply directly to distributed systems, integration monitoring and operational support.

practical_leverage.reason: The model can immediately reduce noisy alerts and clarify which telemetry is for detection, diagnosis, dashboards or human interruption.

compression_loss.reason: The chapter contains additional depth on tails, measurement resolution and monitoring implementation that becomes valuable when building a complete production system.
